The films exhibit strong UV–vis absorption and violet–blue fluorescence with a peak maximum around 440 nm and a quantum yield of 84% at 1.5 wt%, with CIE 1931 chromaticity coordinates of (x, y) ≈ (0.17, 0.05). Tauc and Ravindra–Penn analyses indicated bandgap narrowing from 4.0 to 2.97 eV and a corresponding refractive-index enhancement from 1.58 for pristine PC to 2.23 at 3 wt% dye loading, surpassing the high-refractive-index biopolymer chitin taken as a natural reference material for light confinement. These films are promising low-cost, sustainable matrices for luminescent solar concentrator windows in UV-rich environments, supporting daylighting and energy-efficient façades, and enabling climate-resilient building envelopes supporting urban SDG targets for clean energy and sustainable cities. Graphical abstract

title: Hydrophilic, hydrophobic, and porous nanosilica as green additives for geotechnical engineering in cold regions
author: Hamidi, Salaheddin
abstract: Freeze-thaw (F-T) cycles in cold regions severely degrade clay soils, leading to reduced strength, increased permeability, and compromised infrastructure stability. While conventional stabilizers like cement and lime are effective, their use is associated with high CO₂ emissions and resource depletion, raising environmental concerns. This study investigates nanosilica (NS) as a sustainable alternative for soil stabilization under F-T conditions. The research specifically evaluates the performance of three distinct nanosilica types—hydrophilic (HPI), hydrophobic (HPO), and porous (P)—with an average particle size of 20–30 nm—to determine how surface chemistry and morphology influence geotechnical behavior. Natural clay samples were treated with 0.5%, 1%, and 1.5% NS and subjected to up to 12 F-T cycles. Unconfined compressive strength (UCS), shear strength, permeability, and microstructural changes were analyzed using UCS, direct shear, falling-head permeability, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) tests. The findings reveal that the optimal choice of nanosilica depends on the engineering objective and exposure to F-T cycles. Under non-freezing conditions, 1% HPI-NS yielded the highest UCS (1.21 MPa, ~ 6.7× higher than untreated clay) due to extensive viscous gel formation. However, after multiple F-T cycles, 1% P-NS demonstrated superior durability (UCS = 0.95 MPa), attributed to nano-whisker development and enhanced matrix resilience. In contrast, 1% HPO-NS produced the lowest permeability across all conditions, owing to its water-repellent nature. SEM images confirmed gel formation and microstructural densification in treated samples. This study provides the first comparative framework for selecting nanosilica type based on application-specific goals—strength enhancement (HPI/P-NS) or permeability control (HPO-NS)—under realistic cold-region conditions. It highlights the potential of nanomaterials as environmentally responsible solutions for resilient geotechnical engineering.

title: Fabrication and performance of CA-PK-PVP membrane for oil-in-water emulsion separation
author: Arshad, Syed Khizer
abstract: The increasing global demand for clean water and the limitations of conventional wastewater treatment technologies have accelerated interest in sustainable membrane-based solutions. In this study, a novel cellulose acetate-poly ketone-polyvinylpyrrolidone (CA-PK-PVP) composite membrane was fabricated through a non-solvent induced phase separation (NIPS) method. The uniqueness of this work lies in the combined use of cellulose acetate as a hydrophilic biopolymer, poly ketone as a mechanically reinforcing and solvent-resistant component, and PVP as a hydrophilic pore-forming agent to tune membrane morphology and separation performance. Different CA: PK ratios (9:1, 8:2, 7:3 and 5:5) were first investigated, and the CA_8-PK_2 membrane showed the best balance between permeability and oil rejection. Further incorporation of PVP significantly enhanced membrane porosity and surface hydrophilicity, leading to the formation of an asymmetric porous structure with improved water transport pathways. The optimized CA_8-PK_2-PVP_5 membrane exhibited a low water contact angle of 42.3° and a high oil contact angle of 124.7°, indicating excellent hydrophilic and oleophobic surface properties. In addition, the membrane showed improved mechanical strength of approximately 23 MPa and good solvent resistance after long-term immersion in ethanol, hexane, isopropanol, and toluene. Among all fabricated membranes, CA_8-PK_2-PVP_5 achieved the optimal separation performance, with a high water flux of 848 L m⁻² h⁻¹ and oil rejection above 99% under a low operating pressure of 100 mbar. The membrane also effectively separated different oil-in-water emulsions, including hexane, toluene, xylene, and petroleum ether, while maintaining stable rejection performance over repeated filtration cycles. These findings demonstrate that the synergistic integration of CA, PK, and PVP provides an effective strategy for preparing high-performance membranes for oily wastewater treatment.

title: Review: MXenes for energy storage and conversion devices—advances in green synthesis, use of machine-learning, and electrochemical response
author: Opia, Anthony Chukwunonso
abstract: Recently, MXenes have become effective electrode materials for devices including batteries, supercapacitors (SCs), sensors, antennas, and optoelectronic devices, as well as for sustainable energy storage. They are promising choices for a variety of energy conversion and storage materials due to their metallic conductivity, good hydrophilicity, and ability to act as ideal templates for developing other materials with tunable features. Recent advances in energy devices and storage using MXene as electrode materials are outlined in this article. The fundamental ideas of energy storage and renovation systems are examined. The following sections highlight the special qualities of Green Synthesis Methods for MXenes. Potential fixes for issues that arose during the development of MXene were investigated, as was the use of Machine learning techniques as cutting-edge approaches to MXene product optimisation. Additionally, MXene's applications in energy conversion devices, such as supercapacitors, catalysis, various batteries, and electrochemical sensing were highlighted. A discussion of potential future opportunities for MXene-based materials in energy industries for sustainable technology wraps up the study.

title: Ultrasonic-Assisted Synthesis of a Gellan/PAA-ZIF-8 Nanocomposite Hydrogel for Efficient Heavy Metals Removal
author: Nemati, Maryam
journal: Journal of Inorganic and Organometallic Polymers and Materials
abstract: In this study, a novel and effective nanocomposite hydrogel based on gellan gum (GG) was created using polyacrylic acid (PAA) and zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) (GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8), which was successfully produced through a sustainable ultrasonic-assisted method. The combination of biopolymer gellan and crystalline ZIF-8 was designed to leverage its hydrophilicity, biocompatibility, and high surface area for the effective removal of toxic heavy metal ions. Comprehensive characterization using FTIR, XRD, and EDS confirmed the successful synthesis of the hydrogel, the efficient integration of ZIF-8 into its structure, and the formation of a porous, semi-crystalline, and thermally stable hybrid network. The synthesized GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8 hydrogel exhibited a swelling ratio of about 1078.8%, a compressive yield of 77.3 MPa, and contained uniformly dispersed ZIF-8 polyhedral particles within the gellan network surface. The GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8 hydrogel was used to remove heavy metal ions (Cd^2+, Pb^2+, and Ni^2+) from water via batch adsorption. Its efficiency depended on pH, and modeling showed a Langmuir isotherm and pseudo-first-order kinetics. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed the process was spontaneous and exothermic. Ultrasonic irradiation improved the dispersion and interaction of ZIF-8 within the gellan network, thereby enhancing adsorption capacity and structural stability. These findings suggest that the GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8 nanocomposite hydrogel is a promising, eco-friendly, and mechanically robust adsorbent for removing heavy metals from contaminated water.

title: Influence of CNT on the mechanical properties of FDM processed PLA nanocomposites
author: Managuli, Sangamesh C.
journal: Journal of The Institution of Engineers (India): Series D
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM), particularly stereolithography (SLA), has revolutionized polymer composite fabrication by enabling high-resolution, geometrically complex components. However, conventional UV-curable resins used in SLA processes often suffer from inadequate mechanical performance, limiting their application in load-bearing and high-wear environments. This study investigates the synthesis of polymer composites with improved mechanical properties by incorporating Titanium Carbide (TiC) particles into a photopolymer resin matrix. SLA was used to create composites with different TiC weight percentages (0%, 0.25%, 0.5%, and 0.75%) under ideal processing circumstances. In compliance with ASTM guidelines, the manufactured samples were assessed for mechanical performance, including tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength and Shore D hardness tests. According to the results, the mechanical properties consistently improve as the TiC content rises. Compared to the unreinforced resin, the 0.75 weight percent TiC composite showed the greatest improvements, increasing its tensile strength by 50%, flexural strength by 73%, and Shore D hardness by 58.8%. The mechanical results were supported by SEM analysis of fracture surfaces, confirming improved interfacial bonding and efficient stress transfer mechanisms by revealing a shift from brittle to ductile failure modes.

title: Development of a Marine Algae-based Facial Cream Enriched With Phycoerythrin: Physicochemical Properties and Biological Activities
author: Kadalmani, Sowmiya
abstract: Phycoerythrin (PE), a marine phycobiliprotein derived from Hypnea valentiae , was extracted, characterized, and evaluated for its potential application in a topical cosmeceutical formulation. The extraction yielded 6.35 mg/g (wet biomass), and spectral analysis confirmed pigment integrity. PE exhibited strong antioxidant activity, with DPPH radical scavenging increasing from 32.4% to 78.6% (20–100 µg/mL) and an IC₅₀ of 46.8 µg/mL, while the ABTS assay showed an IC₅₀ of 41.3 µg/mL. Anti-inflammatory activity revealed IC₅₀ values of 52.1 µg/mL (PE extract) and 60.5 µg/mL (PE cream), compared to 46.6 µg/mL for diclofenac sodium. Antimicrobial analysis demonstrated concentration-dependent activity. HV-PE showed moderate inhibition, whereas the PE-infused cream exhibited enhanced efficacy, with zones of inhibition up to 1.77 cm ( Staphylococcus aureus ), 1.81 cm ( Bacillus subtilis ), 1.96 cm ( Escherichia coli ), and 2.11 cm ( Staphylococcus epidermidis ) at 1000 µg/mL. MIC/MBC values further confirmed improved antibacterial performance of the cream (e.g., S. aureus : 52.34/46.21 µg/mL) compared to HV-PE. The formulated cream showed suitable physicochemical properties, with pH 7.12 (control: 7.48) and improved spreadability (80.71 g·cm/s vs. 74.79 g·cm/s). The SPF increased from 12.08 (control) to 24.04 (PE cream). Zebrafish toxicity studies indicated no observable adverse effects, confirming biocompatibility. Overall, PE demonstrates significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and photoprotective properties, supporting its application as a multifunctional cosmeceutical ingredient. Graphical Abstract

title: Binder Jetting of Fe-50Ni Complex Cores for Enhanced Soft Magnetic Performance
author: Soylemez, Emrecan
abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing offers efficient material usage and enables customized shape designs that are difficult to achieve with conventional methods. This study investigates the binder jetting of Fe-50Ni soft magnetic alloys, which are widely used in transformers, inductors, and motors due to their high flux saturation. The process evaluation focuses on the final densities and magnetic properties of both bulk and complex toroidal designs. Two Fe-50Ni powders with different particle size distributions were processed and sintered under both atmospheric and vacuum conditions. Sintering temperatures near 1360 °C enabled near-full densification, whereas 1335 °C produced geometrically stable parts for complex designs with ~ 80% density, suitable for toroidal inductors. Magnetic characterization showed that binder-jetted bulk toroid samples reached saturation flux densities comparable to a commercial reference at 50 Hz but exhibited broader hysteresis loops due to eddy current loss. In contrast, complex geometries incorporating cavities and segmented designs provided clear benefits, with concentric square-ring designs achieving the highest permeability and highest inductance up to ~ 7 kHz. These results confirm the feasibility of binder jetting for producing Fe-50Ni soft magnetic cores and highlight the potential of geometry-based design strategies to mitigate core losses and enable advanced electrical and electronic applications. Graphical abstract

title: Lignin-Assisted NiO Nanocomposite Electrode for High-Performance Supercapacitors: Structural Insights and Charge Storage Mechanism
author: Deniz, Ali Rıza
journal: Journal of Inorganic and Organometallic Polymers and Materials
abstract: The development of sustainable electrode materials requires the integration of renewable components without compromising electrochemical kinetics or structural durability. Herein, a NiO/lignin nanocomposite was prepared through lignin-assisted hydrothermal synthesis followed by thermal treatment at 350 °C. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of cubic NiO crystallites within a thermally transformed lignin-derived matrix containing residual aromatic and oxygen-bearing functionalities. The composite exhibited an average particle size of approximately 33 nm, a BET surface area of 86.4 m^2 g^−1, a total pore volume of 0.31 cm^3 g^−1, and a mesopore diameter centred at approximately 8.7 nm. The higher surface area and pore volume relative to pristine NiO support the structure-regulating effect of lignin incorporation. Electrochemical performance was evaluated in 1 M KOH using a three-electrode configuration, with pristine NiO and pristine lignin electrodes examined under identical fabrication and testing conditions. The NiO/lignin electrode delivered a specific capacitance of 812 F g^−1 at 1 A g^−1 and retained 74.1% of this value at 20 A g^−1. Its equivalent series and charge-transfer resistances were 0.82 and 3.35 Ω, respectively, indicating reduced ohmic losses and facilitated interfacial charge transfer. The anodic and cathodic b-values of 0.84 and 0.79, together with the Dunn analysis, revealed a mixed charge-storage mechanism involving surface-controlled and diffusion-dependent Faradaic contributions. Moreover, the electrode retained 94.2% of its initial capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.1% after 5000 cycles. The combined structural, kinetic, and control-electrode results indicate that NiO provides the primary Ni^2+/Ni^3+ redox sites, whereas the lignin-derived matrix improves particle dispersion, electrolyte accessibility, interfacial transport, and cycling stability. These findings establish the NiO/lignin nanocomposite as a promising electrode material while recognizing that its practical device performance requires further validation in a mass-balanced two-electrode configuration.

title: Chitosan-Based Haemostatic Systems (Axiostat): An Integrated Approach to Post-operative Wound Management in Vascular Surgery
author: Perri, Paolo
abstract: The effective management of perioperative and post-traumatic bleeding is critical to preventing severe complications, shock, and fatal outcomes. In this context, chitosan emerges as a premier polymeric biomaterial due to its exceptional biochemical properties and inherent hemostatic nature. Among commercially available solutions, the Axiostat sponge stands out as a promising device for promoting hemostasis at surgical and endovascular access sites. This study aimed to conduct a comprehensive chemical-physical characterization of the Axiostat device. The investigation sought to quantify its antioxidant capacity, antibacterial activity, and swelling ratio upon contact with biological fluids—all critical parameters for clot stability and infection prevention. The evaluation was conducted through a multi-scale approach: in vitro Cytotoxicity tests on human adult epidermal keratinocytes (HaCaT) cell lines confirmed the material's biocompatibility. Results demonstrated significant antibacterial activity, with particularly marked efficacy against the pathogen Klebsiella pneumoniae. In vivo application on patients undergoing endovascular procedures validated the device’s effectiveness in the secure closure of arterial access sites. The analysis demonstrates that the Axiostat sponge does not merely act as a mechanical barrier but as a multifunctional medical device. The combination of excellent hemostatic properties, biocompatibility, and antibacterial capacity renders it a high-value clinical tool for optimizing post-operative recovery and reducing infectious complications.

title: Cellular assemblies as living therapeutics
author: Gaspar, Vítor M.
abstract: Multicellular assemblies exhibit emergent, collective behaviours, such as coordinated sensing, self-regulation and self-organization, which make them fundamentally distinct from single-cell therapies. Therapeutic cellular assemblies can be engineered at multiple hierarchical levels, ranging from individual cells to linear, planar and volumetric units, using both biological and physical fabrication toolkits. Programming cellular assemblies enables tailored biological functions, leveraging control over cell–cell interactions, tissue-like organization and dynamic responses to microenvironmental cues. Hierarchical cell assemblies can provide therapeutic benefits, but benchmarking against free-cell suspensions or dispersed cells delivered in biomaterials is key to evaluating their performance. Successful clinical translation will require scalable biomanufacturing, robust longitudinal characterization and predictive modelling, ensuring reliable design and function of programmable cellular assemblies. Multicellular assemblies can sense and respond to biochemical and biophysical cues. They can also self-regulate and self-organize, giving rise to emergent behaviours over time. These features make cellular assemblies interesting therapeutic tools for applications such as tissue regeneration and immunomodulation. In this Review, we discuss the design space for therapeutic cellular assemblies, outlining hierarchical building blocks, including single cells and linear, planar and volumetric units, as well as physical and biological toolboxes for their fabrication and functional programming. We examine the biological features of hierarchical cell assemblies, analysing their potential therapeutic benefits, when benchmarked in relation to free-cell suspensions and dispersed cells delivered in biomaterials. Finally, we highlight applications of cellular assemblies in regenerative medicine, immunomodulation and production of biological mediators and discuss translational considerations, including scalable manufacturing, longitudinal characterization and predictive modelling approaches required to engineer cellular assemblies with programmable biological functions. Multicellular assemblies can be programmed to exhibit emergent behaviours that make them promising therapeutic tools, particularly for tissue regeneration and immunomodulation. This Review outlines the design principles, biological advantages and translational requirements for engineering hierarchical cellular assemblies with programmable functions and emphasizes the need for benchmarking them against single-cell and biomaterial-based approaches.

title: Characteristics of femtosecond laser-induced micro-nano topological structures on 7075 aluminum alloy surface
author: Li, Si
abstract: A single-step femtosecond laser processing strategy was employed to induce two-tier micro-nano topological structures on the surface of 7075 aluminum alloy, and their effects on surface wettability, surface hardness, and dry sliding tribological behavior were investigated. The laser-induced composite structure, consisting of micrometer-scale papillae and nanoscale laser-induced periodic surface structures, reduces the actual contact area between water droplets and the substrate while promoting the adsorption of hydrocarbon species, thereby imparting hydrophobic properties. A maximum static contact angle of 164° was achieved, with a sliding angle of 2.7° and a contact angle hysteresis of 7°, reaching a superhydrophobic state. Furthermore, the micro-nano structured surface demonstrated good hydrophobic durability during abrasive impact tests. The experimental results confirm that the femtosecond laser-induced micro-nano structures increase the surface hardness by up to 39% compared to the untreated sample. The grooves within the micro-nano structures can trap wear debris generated during sliding, mitigating abrasive wear. Compared to the untreated surface, the coefficient of friction and wear rate of the laser-treated surfaces were reduced by up to 29% and 44%, respectively. This study provides a feasible pathway for tailoring the wettability and durability of 7075 aluminum alloy surfaces using femtosecond laser micro-nano fabrication, demonstrating potential applications in aerospace, marine equipment, and other related fields.

title: Fabrication of Carbon Quantum Dot-Embedded Polymer Hydrogel Beads for Efficient Dye and Iodine Removal from Wastewater
author: Tadmadge, Rutuja B.
abstract: The release of persistent and dangerous dyes into aquatic environments poses significant hazards to human health and ecosystems due to their toxicity and resistance to adsorption. In this research, a novel composite adsorbent composed of polycarbazole (PCB) and carbon quantum dots (CQDs) encapsulated within sodium alginate (SA) beads (SA@CQD/PCB) was successfully synthesized and applied to remove dyes [direct black (DB), methylene violet (MV) and basic Victoria blue (BVB)] as well as iodine (I_2) from aqueous solutions. Initial dye concentrations of 50 ppm for MV, BVB, and DB and 200 ppm for I_2 were used in adsorption tests, achieving maximum removal efficiencies of 99.25%, 95.07%, 86.98%, and 86.37%, respectively. The superior adsorption performance is attributed to the synergistic interaction between CQDs and PCB, which provides abundant active sites for interactions and promotes π–π interactions. Kinetic studies revealed that the adsorption process followed the pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R^2 = 0.9995), indicating chemisorption as the dominant adsorption mechanism. The Langmuir isotherm analysis revealed a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of 479 mg/gm for MV, demonstrating the excellent adsorption performance of the SA@CQD/PCB hydrogel beads. Furthermore, the practical potential of SA@CQD/PCB beads for large-scale wastewater treatment could be investigated in future studies to assess the feasibility of scaling up the adsorption process. All things considered, this work demonstrates the efficacy of adsorption-based techniques using sustainable composite materials for the removal of both cationic and anionic contaminant dyes, as well as I_2, from contaminated water. Graphical Abstract

title: Formulation and In vitro Characterization of Rosuvastatin Calcium Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Sustained Drug Release
author: Sarwer, Muhammad Umer
abstract: Rosuvastatin calcium (RST) is a BCS class II antihyperlipidemic drug with poor aqueous solubility, which limits its oral performance. The present study aimed to develop and characterize RST-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (CTS-NPs) using the ionic gelation method to improve physicochemical properties and achieve sustained drug release. Nanoparticles were prepared using chitosan and sodium tripolyphosphate (TPP) as a cross-linking agent via ionic gelation and were evaluated for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, morphology, drug loading, entrapment efficiency, and in vitro drug release behavior. The optimized formulation exhibited a nanosized particle diameter of approximately 243.7 nm with a positive zeta potential of about + 30 mV, indicating good colloidal stability. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed spherical and uniformly distributed nanoparticles. Entrapment efficiency ranged from 65.80% to 93.08%, depending on formulation composition. FTIR, DSC, and XRD analyses confirmed successful drug incorporation without chemical incompatibility and revealed partial amorphization of RST within the polymeric matrix. In vitro release studies demonstrated an initial burst followed by sustained drug release up to 24 h, best fitting the Higuchi kinetic model, indicating diffusion-controlled release. These findings suggest that RST-loaded chitosan nanoparticles represent a promising oral nanocarrier system with sustained release characteristics and the potential to improve the oral performance of poorly water-soluble drugs such as rosuvastatin calcium.

title: Molten salt–assisted thermoelectric conversion of biomass for high-capacitance carbon materials
author: Ji, Deqiang
abstract: The growing global energy crisis and increasing greenhouse gas emissions necessitate the development of sustainable energy technologies. However, existing methods for synthesizing biomass-derived carbon materials suffer from limitations such as poor conductivity during low-temperature carbonization, high energy consumption during high-temperature activation, and the need for corrosive reagents, resulting in suboptimal electrochemical performance of the carbon materials. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel composite thermoelectric dual-field electrochemical technology that converts lignin into high-capacitance carbon materials under low-temperature conditions (550 ℃). Using alkali lignin and poplar leaves as raw materials, the products obtained through pyrolysis (2 h) and electrolysis (4 h, 2.8 V) exhibited specific surface areas of 286 and 388 m^2 g^− 1, respectively. In a three-electrode system, the specific capacitance at a current density of 0.5 A g^− 1 reached 230 and 177 F g^− 1; at a current density of 0.1 A g^− 1, the specific capacitance reached 343 and 270 F g^− 1. Furthermore, the resulting materials exhibited excellent rate capability and cycling stability; after 5,000 charge-discharge cycles in a 6 M KOH aqueous solution at a current density of 5 A g^− 1, the capacitance retention rates reached 99.6% and 99.5%, respectively. This molten salt-assisted thermoelectric dual-field method provides a new approach for the low-temperature, efficient preparation of porous carbon materials for biomass-based supercapacitors. Graphical Abstract

title: Rice Protein as an Alternative Ingredient for Sustainable Food Formulations: Nutritional Quality, Functional Properties, Health-promoting Potential, and Emerging Applications
author: Meza, Silvia Leticia Rivero
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable and nutritionally adequate protein sources has intensified interest in alternative plant proteins capable of supporting future food systems. However, many conventional plant proteins still present limitations related to allergenicity, digestibility, sensory quality, and functional performance, highlighting the need for novel sustainable ingredients. In this context, rice protein has emerged as a promising alternative due to its hypoallergenic nature, gluten-free composition, relatively high digestibility, suitability for specialized dietary applications, favorable techno-functional characteristics, and compatibility with sustainable food production systems. This review provides an integrated perspective on rice protein by critically discussing its nutritional quality, techno-functional properties, health-promoting potential, emerging food applications, and contribution to sustainable food systems, thereby addressing knowledge that has remained fragmented across previous reviews. Recent scientific studies addressing protein composition, digestibility, bioactive peptides, processing technologies, and applications in plant-based foods and nutraceutical systems were critically analyzed. Current evidence demonstrated that rice proteins and rice-derived peptides exhibit antioxidant, antihypertensive, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, and immunomodulatory activities, while recent advances in protein modification technologies have significantly improved solubility, emulsification, gelation, and structuring properties. Furthermore, the valorization of rice bran and broken rice supports circular economy strategies and sustainable food production. In this way, rice protein represents a strategic ingredient for the development of next-generation functional foods and sustainable health-oriented dietary systems.

title: Ligand-independent EPHA2 signaling sustains neural progenitors via ECSIT and NAD^+
author: Diem Nghi, Tran
abstract: EPHA2 sustains embryonic cortical progenitors by coupling apical receptor signaling to ECSIT-dependent Complex I activity and mitochondrial NAD^+, providing a functional link between cell surface receptor state and mitochondrial redox control during corticogenesis. Ligand-independent EPHA2 signaling is required for cortical progenitor maintenance in vivo. EPHA2 perturbation reduces mitochondrial respiration, Complex I activity, NAD^+ regeneration, and mitochondrial ECSIT abundance. Restoring mitochondrial NAD^+ regeneration or mitochondrial ECSIT attenuates progenitor defects caused by EPHA2 disruption. A PP2A-sensitive ECSIT phospho-state, including T179, links EPHA2 signaling to mitochondrial ECSIT accumulation. EPHA2 sustains embryonic cortical progenitors by coupling apical receptor signaling to ECSIT-dependent Complex I activity and mitochondrial NAD^+, providing a functional link between cell surface receptor state and mitochondrial redox control during corticogenesis. Embryonic neural stem and progenitor cells occupy a specialized niche along the lateral ventricles, where receptors on their apical membrane sense extracellular cues essential for preserving progenitor identity. How such surface signals are coupled to mitochondrial metabolism remains unclear. Here, we identify EPHA2 as a receptor enriched in cortical progenitors and show that disruption of its non-canonical, ligand-independent signaling compromises progenitor maintenance in vivo. EPHA2 perturbation reduces mitochondrial respiration, Complex I activity, and mitochondrial NAD^+ regeneration, and is accompanied by lower mitochondrial abundance of the Complex I assembly factor ECSIT. Restoring mitochondrial NAD^+ regeneration with MTS- Lb NOX, or restoring mitochondrial ECSIT with ECSIT WT—but not a mitochondrial targeting-deficient mutant—attenuates the progenitor defects caused by EPHA2 perturbation. Maternal supplementation with NAD^+ or its precursor NMN similarly mitigates these developmental defects. We further identify a PP2A-sensitive ECSIT phospho-state, including T179, that is consistent with regulated mitochondrial ECSIT accumulation downstream of EPHA2. Together, these findings support a model in which EPHA2 helps maintain embryonic cortical progenitors by sustaining ECSIT-dependent Complex I-linked mitochondrial redox homeostasis.

title: Dextran-based biodegradable film reinforced with glycerol and isomalto-oligosaccharides: characterization and preservation performance on strawberry
author: Zhang, Yao
journal: Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization
abstract: An eco-friendly biodegradable film (DGI) was fabricated using dextran, glycerol, and isomalto-oligosaccharides (IMO); The DGI film exhibited desirable mechanical and barrier abilities, with good molecular compatibility and thermal stability; The DGI film outperformed commercial polyethylene film in preserving the quality of fresh strawberries. Microbially derived polysaccharides have attracted considerable attention for developing sustainable bio-based food packaging materials. In this study, a dextran-based composite film (DGI) incorporating glycerol and isomalto-oligosaccharides was fabricated and characterized. The DGI film exhibited improved mechanics with an elongation at bread of 44.17 ± 3.08% and tensile strength of 5.40 ± 2.60 MPa. It also showed favorable water vapor permeability ((46.94 ± 2.78) ×10^− 11 g·m/(m²·s·Pa)), high light transmittance and water solubility. Scanning electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analyses confirmed its excellent molecular compatibility and enhanced thermal stability. During strawberry storage, the DGI film outperformed commercial polyethylene film in preserving quality, as evidenced by a more intact appearance, brighter color, and higher firmness. It also effectively inhibited the losses of in soluble solids, organic acids, and ascorbic acid, while delaying visible mold development. This study provides a theoretical basis and technical support for the applications of dextran-based biodegradable films in fruit preservation. Graphical abstract

title: Fish skin–derived collagen–chitosan composite membranes: Structure, properties, and packaging performance
author: Dang, Nhan Thi Thanh
abstract: Sustainable and bio-based polymer materials are increasingly investigated as alternatives to synthetic plastics. In this study, type I collagen was extracted from catfish ( Pangasius bocourti ) skin, a seafood processing byproduct, and blended with chitosan to fabricate collagen–chitosan composite membranes. The structure and properties of the membranes were systematically characterized in terms of morphology, intermolecular interactions, thermal stability, water resistance, and antibacterial functionality. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed composition-dependent microstructural features, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) indicated intermolecular interactions between collagen and chitosan chains. The composite membranes exhibited enhanced thermal stability and reduced water solubility with increasing structural compatibility. The functional performance of the optimized membrane was further evaluated using persimmons ( Diospyros kaki ) as a model system under refrigerated storage conditions, demonstrating reduced moisture loss and delayed visible deterioration compared with unwrapped controls. The results illustrate how structure–property relationships govern the functional behavior of collagen–chitosan composites and highlight the potential of fish skin–derived collagen as a sustainable biopolymer resource. Type I collagen was successfully extracted from catfish skin and blended with chitosan to form composite membranes. Intermolecular interactions between collagen and chitosan governed the microstructure and thermal stability of the composites. Composite membranes exhibited improved water resistance and antibacterial functionality compared with neat collagen. The optimized membrane demonstrated effective moisture barrier performance under refrigerated storage conditions.

title: Laser-induced surface texturing and nanomaterial functionalization of PLA/PHBV surfaces for enhanced cell adhesion
author: Queiroz, Rafaela Campos
abstract: Current research on the development of biomaterials aims at reducing bacterial colonization and increasing cell adhesion on the surface of implantable devices for regenerative medicine. Equally noteworthy is the growing interest in using materials from renewable sources and biodegradable in medical devices. In this study, femtosecond laser surface texturing was applied to PLA/PHBV polymer blends nanocomposites with and without cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) fillings. Micro-pillar structures were developed using a femtosecond laser. The textured samples were characterized by SEM, profilometry, and contact angle measurements. The effect of texturing on cytotoxicity, cell adhesion and proliferation were evaluated by MTT assay and confocal fluorescence microscopy by using L929 fibroblasts cell line. The results showed that laser texturing led to a significant increase in surface roughness and caused the material to change from hydrophilic to hydrophobic behavior, a phenomenon explained by the Wenzel model. The polymers showed higher cell viability and directional growth after laser treatment, especially in the samples containing 0.5–1.5 wt% CNT and up to 5 wt% CNC. However, it was observed that at high concentrations of nanofillers the biocompatibility was compromised, which could be attributed to particle agglomeration and percolation effects. Overall, this study highlights the synergistic role of laser-induced microstructures and functionalization with nanomaterials in modulating the surface properties of biopolymers to promote biocompatibility, offering a promising approach for the development of bioactive surfaces for high-performance implants.

title: Advances In the Valorization of Avocado By-Products: Bioactive Compounds, Techno-Functional Properties, and Structure–Function Relationships
author: Perucini-Avendaño, Madeleine
abstract: Avocado ( Persea americana Mill.) processing generates large amounts of peel and seed that remain underutilized despite their potential as functional food ingredients. While previous reviews have focused mainly on the chemical composition and antioxidant capacity of avocado by-products, less attention has given to the role of tissue-specific microstructure and ripening-related structural changes in determining their techno-functional behavior. This review critically integrates recent advances in the valorization of avocado by-products, with particular emphasis on peel and seed as sources of bioactive compounds and techno-functional ingredients. It examines the chemical composition, microstructural organization, and physicochemical transformations of these by-products, highlighting how their structural features influence functional performance. Special attention is given to phenolic compounds, dietary fiber, and associated polysaccharides, and to how cell wall architecture, pectin solubilization, and tissue disassembly influence the techno-functional properties of ingredients obtained from avocado by-products. These properties, such as water- and oil-holding capacities, emulsifying properties, and gelation behavior, are primarily evaluated after processing the by-products into functional food ingredients. Additionally, the review discusses the impact of processing and extraction strategies on structural integrity, bioactive retention, and techno-functional functionality, as well as recent advances in food-grade applications, bioaccessibility, safety considerations, and current challenges for industrial implementation. Overall, this review provides an integrated framework that links composition, microstructure, processing, and functionality to support the sustainable valorization of avocado by-products as value-added food ingredients.

title: Sustainable Avocado Seed Starch Nanoparticles for Limonene Encapsulation: A Novel Immunomodulatory Delivery System
author: Alves, Guilherme L.
journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
abstract: D-limonene is a bioactive monoterpene with recognized antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, whose therapeutic application is severely constrained by its high volatility, sensitivity to oxidation, and poor aqueous solubility. Nanoencapsulation within biopolymeric matrices represents a promising strategy to overcome these limitations. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and characterize chemically modified avocado seed ( Persea americana Miller) starch nanoparticles, produced via a simple one-step nanoprecipitation method, for D-limonene encapsulation, evaluating their physicochemical properties, long-term stability, and immunomodulatory potential. Acetylation of the starch was confirmed by FTIR, ¹³C NMR, and degree of substitution (DS) determination, which collectively demonstrated successful introduction of acetyl groups into the polymer backbone and the resulting increase in hydrophobicity that underlies the encapsulation capacity of the nanocarrier. Thermogravimetric analysis further characterized the physicochemical properties of the modified starch and nanoparticles. The resulting nanoparticles displayed mean diameters lower than 350 nm, predominantly homogeneous size distributions (PdI < 0.3), zeta potentials ranging from − 10.46 to − 13.77 mV and encapsulation efficiency higher than 80% in two formulations. Long-term stability assessment demonstrated preservation of colloidal integrity after 10 months under refrigerated storage, with retention of approximately 69% of initial encapsulation efficiency. TEM analysis revealed small, globular particles with smooth surfaces and narrow size distribution, while FT-IR spectroscopy provided surface chemistry characterization consistent with limonene confinement within the nanoparticle core. In vitro release studies demonstrated a sustained, gradual release profile, with 59.1% of the encapsulated DL released after 24 h and release kinetics best described by a first-order model, with Fickian diffusion as the dominant transport mechanism. Immunological analysis demonstrated a potent and context-dependent immunomodulatory potential of ASNP-DL1. In vitro assays showed the suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6) in macrophages and dendritic cells, concurrently maintaining anti-inflammatory IL-10 at basal levels, indicating a coordinated shift toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. These findings underscore the potential of this sustainable nanocarrier as a versatile platform that effectively addresses the physicochemical limitations of D-limonene, positioning this sustainable, agriculturally-derived nanocarrier as a promising candidate for immunomodulatory therapies with broad pharmaceutical and biotechnological relevance.

title: Catechol modified sodium alginate/gelatin films reinforced with bio-mediated HNTs for enhanced wound healing applications
author: Ambrose, Anishia
abstract: The increasing prevalence of wounds caused by various causes that can cause complications in the everyday activities of humans is a significant worldwide health issue. Despite recent progress, there remains a substantial demand for efficient wound healing materials, especially for persistent and challenging wounds. The objective of the present work is to design a feasible, viable and efficient wound healing material. Sodium Alginate (SA) has been adopted for its remarkable cell viability and effectiveness in promoting wound healing. It is modified using catechol to enhance cell adhesion and to improve healing. Catechol modified sodium alginate is then blended with gelatin and leucas aspera leaf extract coated halloysite nano tubes (HNT). Leucas aspera is chosen for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The Modified-HNT@catechol-SA/gelatin film is formulated by adopting the solvent casting technique. The resultant films were characterized for functional group changes using FT-IR, crystallinity by XRD, elemental composition by XPS, thermal stability via TGA and hydrophilicity and swelling ratio. The Modified-HNT@catechol-SA/gelatin film showed higher ZOI of about 18 mm and 19 mm against E. coli and S. aureus , antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential (> 50%), MTT assay showed > 90% of cell viability against L929 cell lines and in-vitro scratch assay revealed 89.5  ±  1.27% of wound closure using L929 cell lines. Based on the findings, it is evident that the developed polymeric nanocomposite thin film will be considered for wound healing applications. Furthermore, the implementation in in-vivo wound healing studies is essential for the validation of the material in clinical applications.

title: Galactomannans from Neltuma spp. as Emerging Functional Dietary Fibre for Human Nutrition: Extraction Technologies and Health Potential
author: Escobar, Adrián
abstract: Galactomannans are reserve polysaccharides widely distributed in legume seeds and recognized for their technological and physiological properties. Their structure, consisting of a β-(1→4)-linked mannose backbone with α-(1→6)-galactose side chains, determines their solubility, viscosity, and functional behavior. In recent years, galactomannans have gained increasing attention as functional dietary fibre due to their potential effects on glycemic regulation, cholesterol reduction, gut microbiota modulation, and short-chain fatty acid production. This review critically analyzes the current knowledge on galactomannans derived from Neltuma spp., a group of underutilized leguminous species native to arid and semi-arid regions of Latin America, particularly the Gran Chaco ecosystem. This review aims to describe the structural characteristics of sources of galactomannans from seeds, extraction and purification technologies, and their potential nutritional implications of Neltuma spp.-derived galactomannans, highlighting their role as sustainable ingredients for human nutrition. Conventional extraction methods, including aqueous and alkaline extraction, are compared with biotechnological approaches such as enzymatic pretreatments, ultrasound-assisted extraction, and membrane technologies, highlighting their effects on yield, purity, and structural preservation. Evidence suggests that Neltuma spp. seeds represent a promising alternative source of food-grade galactomannans with potential applications as sustainable hydrocolloids and functional ingredients. However, studies regarding their digestibility, microbiota interactions, and clinical effects remain limited. The valorization of Neltuma spp. may contribute to the diversification of dietary fibre sources while supporting sustainable bioeconomy strategies and regional food innovation in Latin America.

title: Next-generation photodynamic cancer therapy: purpurin-based nanocarriers as emerging photosensitizers
author: Dudhwala, Yash D.
abstract: Cancer remains a leading global health burden, with approximately 20 million new cases and 9.7 million deaths reported in 2022, and projections indicating a substantial rise by 2050. Nearly one in five individuals is expected to develop cancer during their lifetime, underscoring the urgent need for more effective and targeted therapies. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a minimally invasive modality that utilizes photosensitizers, light, and oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) for localized tumor destruction. However, conventional photosensitizers are limited by poor solubility, low tumor selectivity, and suboptimal photostability. This review critically examines purpurin-18 and related chlorin-based nanocarriers as next-generation photosensitizer systems for PDT. Although their names are similar, purpurin-18 is chemically distinct from natural anthraquinone purpurin and is classified as a chlorin-type tetrapyrrolic macrocycle. Due to its red-light absorption, ROS-generating capacity, and chemical modifiability, purpurin-18 has shown improved therapeutic potential when incorporated into nanocarrier systems. Nanocarrier engineering significantly improves photosensitizer dispersibility, stability, and tumor targeting, enabling enhanced intracellular uptake and apoptosis induction across multiple cancer models. Despite promising preclinical outcomes, challenges related to safety, biodistribution, standardized photophysical characterization, and clinical translation persist. Future directions include the development of stimuli-responsive systems, combinatorial therapeutic strategies, and AI-assisted nanocarrier optimization to advance purpurin-18-based nano-PDT toward clinical applicability. Graphical Abstract

title: Graphene oxide/SPEEK nanocomposite proton exchange membranes for enhanced bioelectricity generation and biofouling resistance in microbial fuel cells
author: Ghasemi, Mostafa
abstract: Microbial Fuel Cells (MFCs) have emerged as a promising technology for simultaneously treating wastewater and generating renewable energy. However, their large-scale application is still limited by the drawbacks of conventional proton exchange membranes, such as Nafion, primarily due to their high cost. Sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) has therefore attracted considerable attention as a lower-cost alternative membrane with good proton conductivity. Nevertheless, pristine SPEEK membranes often suffer from excessive swelling and limited mechanical stability. To overcome these limitations, nanocomposite membranes incorporating graphene oxide (GO) have been developed to improve structural stability and electrochemical performance. In this study, SPEEK membranes incorporating GO nanosheets were developed as a cost-effective, high-performance alternative. GO was introduced into the SPEEK matrix at loadings ranging from 0.5 to 3.0 wt%, and the resulting nanocomposite membranes were systematically characterized by various spectroscopy and microscopy techniques. Among the prepared samples, the membrane containing 2.0 wt% GO exhibited the most balanced physicochemical properties, including a proton conductivity of 0.089 S cm^−1 at 30 °C, a water uptake of 34.2%, and an ion exchange capacity of 1.62 meq g^−1. When evaluated in a dual-chamber MFC system, this optimized membrane achieved a maximum power density of 480 mW m^−2, a Coulombic efficiency of 47.3%, and a COD removal efficiency of 94.6% within 72 hours of operation. Furthermore, long-term stability testing over 60 days demonstrated only a 7.2% reduction in performance, indicating significantly improved stability compared with Nafion 117 under identical operating conditions. Surface analysis revealed reduced biofouling on the SPEEK/GO membrane, indicating improved resistance to microbial adhesion. These findings demonstrate that incorporating GO into SPEEK is an effective strategy for enhancing membrane performance and durability in MFC applications.

title: Haemodynamic control of zonated liver function via instructive vascular Wnt signalling
author: Lee, Ki Hong
abstract: The study identified blood flow as the key signal that programs liver blood vessels to instruct liver function through WNT signalling. The vascular endothelium forms a systemically disseminated organ that translates micromilieu factors into instructive cues, designated as angiocrine signalling. While vascular control of organ function mechanisms have been discovered in essentially all major organs, the mechanisms of translating milieu factors into angiocrine signalling mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here, focussing on the well-established angiocrine Wnt signalling-regulated liver metabolic zonation paradigm, we identified blood flow-induced haemodynamic stress as a biophysical sensor that governs the angiocrine expression profile of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSEC). Combining single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial proteomics, we generated a high-resolution crosstalk map of LSEC and hepatocytes from LSEC Wnt-deficient mutant mice and littermate controls. Intriguingly, vascular Wnt receptors, in parallel with angiocrine Wnt ligands, were specifically enriched in pericentral LSEC, enforcing the spatially coordinated vascular Wnt functions. Consequently, vascular Wnt further modulated angiocrine gene signatures, LSEC morphology, and the expression of gap junctional molecules in an autocrine manner. Taken together, the data define LSEC as a dynamic cellular decoder that translates biophysical forces into instructive angiocrine signals via activating promiscuous vascular Wnt factors.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of Calcium Pectinate Hydrogel Formulations: A Stacked Ensemble Framework for Alpha-Lipoic Acid–β-Cyclodextrin Oral Delivery System Design
author: Raj, Karikalachsozhan Prakash
abstract: Background Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a major complication of diabetes mellitus, affecting nearly 30–50% of diabetic patients worldwide. Although α-Lipoic acid (ALA) demonstrates significant antioxidant potential in DPN management, its clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, photochemical instability, and variable oral bioavailability. Complexation with β-cyclodextrin (βCD) may improve these physicochemical limitations; however, optimization of calcium pectinate hydrogel carriers remains challenging due to complex concentration-dependent interactions. Objective This study aimed to develop a stacked ensemble machine learning (ML) framework for predicting critical quality attributes of calcium pectinate hydrogels and to apply the model for rational design of an ALA–βCD oral delivery system. Methods A meta-dataset containing 91 formulation data points was curated from 10 peer-reviewed studies on calcium pectinate hydrogels. Fourteen engineered physicochemical features were derived from pectin and CaCl₂ concentrations. A leakage-free stacked ensemble comprising artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF), and XGBoost base learners with a Ridge regression meta-learner was evaluated using nested 5-fold cross-validation and pseudo-external validation. Virtual screening of 10,000 candidate formulations was conducted using the Derringer–Suich desirability function. FTIR spectroscopy and in silico ADMET profiling were performed to characterise the ALA–βCD inclusion complex. Results The stacked ensemble achieved cross-validated R² values of 0.93 for hardness, 0.91 for drug content, and 0.87 for T80, outperforming all baseline models. Pseudo-external validation confirmed satisfactory generalisation (mean R² = 0.89). SHAP analysis identified the egg-box stoichiometric ratio and crosslinking density index as dominant predictors of gel hardness. Virtual screening identified an optimal formulation region at pectin 5.7–6.4% w/v and CaCl₂ 1.5–2.0% w/v. FTIR confirmed successful ALA–βCD inclusion complex formation, while ADMET analysis demonstrated favorable oral drug-likeness and safety characteristics. Conclusion The proposed ML framework provides a robust and physically interpretable strategy for calcium pectinate formulation optimization and establishes a computationally guided foundation for ALA–βCD oral delivery system development.

title: Prognostic factors and predictive modeling of in-hospital mortality among MDRO-positive inpatients: a retrospective cohort and GBD MICROBE study
author: Jiang, Fan
abstract: Existing studies on prognostic prediction for multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) are limited by single-model designs, incomplete consideration of ward environmental observations, and insufficient linkage to national antimicrobial-resistance burden data. This single-center pilot study aimed to identify interpretable prognostic factors for in-hospital mortality among MDRO-positive inpatients, internally evaluate a prognostic model in the non-surgical cohort, describe bed-unit environmental bacterial isolates, and compare local MDRO-related observations with national resistance-burden data. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1057 MDRO-positive inpatients from 2019 to 2023. The non-surgical cohort was split into 7:3 training and validation sets. Seven machine-learning and statistical models were assessed via fivefold cross-validation. Strict statistical criteria (99.5% CIs, P  < 0.005) were adopted for multivariable Cox regression analysis, with covariates selected based on clinical evidence and conservative screening. Environmental monitoring covered 84 bed units across three departments, and GBD 2023 data were used for national burden comparison. Advanced age and higher comorbidity/diagnosis burden were the most consistent internally validated prognostic factors associated with in-hospital mortality in the overall and non-surgical cohorts. Cumulative antibiotic use and urethral catheterization variables lost significance after correction. The XGBoost Cox model achieved the best internal discrimination (training C-index = 0.814, validation C-index = 0.807), whereas conventional Cox regression offered better clinical interpretability. Environmental monitoring identified variation in colony counts and environmental bacterial-isolate detection across bed-unit sites, and local MDRO-related observations were compared descriptively with national high-burden pathogens. Age and comorbidity burden were the most consistent internally validated prognostic factors for in-hospital mortality among MDRO-positive inpatients. Because the cohort was defined by laboratory-recorded MDRO detection and clinical infection could not be independently confirmed for every patient, colonization and infection may have been mixed. The environmental and GBD analyses provide exploratory and surveillance context, respectively; multicenter external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Integrated Thermo-Mechanical Behavior of Mediterranean Agro-Waste Fiber/Epoxy Biocomposites for Energy-Efficient Building Applications
author: Jawarneh, Ali M.
abstract: Sustainable bio-composites were progressively considered as an eco-friendly alternative for sustainable building and energy saving materials. However, their proper evaluations regarding various characteristics are still required to develop their commercial implementations. This work systematically investigates and illuminates the capabilities of various Mediterranean natural fiber epoxy composites for sustainable building and energy saving materials. Various composites with different reinforcement conditions were developed and examined regarding mechanical performance including tensile strength, elastic modulus, strain, bending, and impact, as well as thermal characteristics including thermal conductivity, volumetric specific heat, and thermal diffusivity. TGA, DTG, FTIR were also performed for the considered fibers to reveal their thermal stability, chemical absorption pattern, and suitability for such composites. SEM was considered to perform morphological analysis of the composites and to justify the gained results. It was approved that all of fig, hay, olive, and grape epoxy composites at fiber content of 15 wt% had revealed desired tensile strength. Superior tensile modulus of elasticity of 5.34 GPa was achieved in case of fig epoxy composite with fiber content of 25 wt%. The composite with 25 wt % of hay fibers demonstrated the best impact resistance property. However, the best bending resistance and the lowest thermal conductivity was in favor of the 15 wt% olive based composites. This in order they would demonstrate the potential of such composites for sustainable building and energy saving materials, as thay have desired integrated mechanical-thermal performance for such applications.

title: Gastro-Retentive Floating Mucoadhesive Zinc Pectinate–Carboxymethyl Cassia Tora Gum IPN Microbeads for Repaglinide: Formulation, Box–Behnken Optimization, and in Vivo Anti-Diabetic Evaluation
author: Kalaskar, Ankita
abstract: Repaglinide (RPG), an oral diabetes medication, acts swiftly but has a short half-life of 1 h, requiring a controlled, extended-release system to maintain therapeutic plasma levels and minimize side effects. This study developed gastro-retentive floating mucoadhesive microbeads (MBs) for prolonged drug release using a cross-linked interpenetrating polymeric network (IPN) of low-methoxy pectin and carboxymethyl cassia tora gum (C-CTG). The formulation was optimized through ionotropic gelation using the response surface methodology with a Box-Behnken design. Optimized RPG-loaded MBs showed 98.2% drug entrapment, 79.65% controlled drug release over 8 h, and buoyancy for over 10 h. Drug transformation from the crystalline to amorphous state was confirmed by diffractograms and thermograms. Laboratory tests confirmed MB stability and floating ability, and animal studies in diabetic rats showed sustained blood sugar-lowering effects. RPG-loaded MBs gradually reduced blood glucose levels, reaching 74.45% after 24 h, unlike the rapid but short-lived effects of the unencapsulated drug. Zinc ions enhanced the mechanical stability and mucoadhesive properties of IPN MB, whereas sodium bicarbonate ensured prolonged gastric buoyancy. These innovative MBs offer a promising gastro-retentive delivery system for RPG, providing extended release, enhanced therapeutic effects, and improved management of type 2 diabetes. Graphical Abstract

title: Clinical efficacy study of LED red and infrared light therapy for chronic non-specific low back pain
author: Yi, Bin
abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of an LED red and infrared light therapy for the treatment of chronic nonspecific low back pain. From September to December 2022, 176 patients diagnosed with chronic non-specific low back pain were enrolled and randomly assigned to two groups: the experimental group ( n  = 89) and the control group ( n  = 87). The experimental group received treatment with the test device (630 + 850 nm, 15 + 6 mW/cm^2) combined with rehabilitation training, whereas the control group received a sham device (630 nm, 1 mW/cm^2) alongside rehabilitation training. After 28 days of treatment, clinical efficacy was assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) score. The total effective rate was 80.90% in the experimental group and 27.59% in the control group, with a rate difference of 53.31%. The experimental group showed significantly better outcomes compared to the control group.( p < 0.0001). The Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) score in the experimental group was significantly higher than that in the control group ( p < 0.0001). No serious adverse events occurred during the trial, and all reported adverse events were unrelated to the device. The LED red and infrared light therapy device may serve as a safe and beneficial intervention for chronic nonspecific low back pain. Trial registration number: ChiCTR2600117704 (Retrospectively registered). Date of registration: 2026-01-28.

title: Removal of Congo red Using Treated Artichoke Stems: Modelling and Optimization of Efficiency via Plackett–Burman Design, Box–Behnken Design and Desirability Function
author: Trachi, Mahmoud
abstract: In the present study, a novel adsorbent was prepared from artichoke stems, an abundant agricultural by-product generated during harvesting and food processing. The adsorbent was characterized using SEM–EDX, BET, and FTIR analyses, and subsequently employed for the removal of Congo red (CR) from synthetic aqueous solutions under batch conditions. Screening experiments based on the Plackett–Burman design (PBD) were conducted to identify the main factors influencing the CR adsorption process. The Box–Behnken design (BBD) combined with the desirability function (DF) was then applied to optimize the key operational variables: initial dye concentration (50–200 mg/L), pH (2–10), temperature (25–45 °C), and adsorbent dosage (1–5 g/L). Based on the resulting second-order polynomial model, the optimal conditions for maximum CR removal were determined. Kinetic and equilibrium studies were performed under these optimized conditions, and adsorption thermodynamics were investigated over the temperature range of 298–318 K. The maximum adsorption efficiency of 97% was achieved at an initial CR concentration of 50 mg/L, pH 5.8, temperature of 45 °C, and adsorbent dosage of 5 g/L. The pseudo-second-order model best described the kinetic data, while both Langmuir and Temkin isotherm models provided an excellent fit to the equilibrium data, indicating a maximum adsorption capacity of 114.9 mg/g at 318 K. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the adsorption process was endothermic and spontaneous. The combined PBD-BBD approach yielded reliable optimization results and achieved high dye removal efficiency, demonstrating the potential for valorization and effective utilization of treated artichoke stems as a sustainable and cost-effective adsorbent for wastewater treatment applications.

title: Response surface optimization and characterization of chitosan nanoparticle/sugar palm starch bionanocomposite films incorporated with butterfly pea extract and reinforced with nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots for food packaging applications
author: Rachmina, Rachmina
journal: Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization
abstract: Biodegradable active films have emerged as sustainable alternatives to petroleum-based packaging materials. This study presents a novel strategy by integrating butterfly pea extract and nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots into a chitosan nanoparticle/sugar palm starch biocomposite film, followed by multi-response optimization using Box–Behnken response surface methodology to simultaneously improve mechanical, barrier, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties ). The effects of CH: SPS ratio, NCQD concentration, and BP concentration on antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus , tensile strength (TS), elongation at break (EB), water vapor permeability (WVP), and antioxidant activity were investigated. The optimized formulation exhibited inhibition zones of 12.67 and 12.34 mm against E. coli and S. aureus , respectively, TS of 117.80 MPa, EB of 13.45%, WVP of 8.15 × 10⁻⁷ g Pa⁻¹ s⁻¹ m⁻¹, and antioxidant activity of 21.55%. Structural characterization revealed molecular interactions among film constituents, modified crystallinity, smoother surface morphology, enhanced thermal stability, and improved UV-barrier properties following the incorporation of BP and NCQDs. Release studies demonstrated controlled diffusion behavior of active compounds in aqueous and ethanol simulants, predominantly described by Higuchi and Korsmeyer–Peppas models. These findings suggest that the optimized CH/SPS/BPE/NCQD biocomposite films possess promising potential for food packaging applications.

title: Fabrication and functional evaluation of polyvinyl alcohol films reinforced with bio-derived silicified microcrystalline cellulose and zinc oxide nanoparticles
author: Thayyullathil, Ajmal
abstract: Biodegradable films with enhanced barrier, UV- shielding, antimicrobial and mechanical properties are highly desirable for food packaging, protective coatings and biomedical applications. In this context, Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA) composite films reinforced with bio-derived Silicified Microcrystalline Cellulose (SMCC) and Zinc Oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles were fabricated to develop biodegradable multifunctional films with enhanced properties. Bare PVA, PVA/MCC and PVA/SMCC films were also fabricated to assess the individual and synergistic effect of Microcrystalline Cellulose, SMCC and ZnO nanoparticles on the overall performances of films. On analysis, PVA/SMCC showed reduced water uptake and water vapour transmission compared to PVA/MCC while PVA/SMCC-ZnO exhibited the lowest moisture absorption by restricting polymer chain mobility. Antibacterial studies revealed no activity for PVA, PVA/MCC and PVA/SMCC, while PVA/SMCC-ZnO film exhibited a distinct inhibition zone of ~ 11 mm against both E. coli and S. aureus, which is attributed to ZnO induced reactive oxygen species generation and membrane disruption. Soil burial studies demonstrated that MCC enhances the biodegradability of PVA, while SMCC and ZnO suppresses the biodegradation due to their antimicrobial nature. FE-SEM analysis supported these findings, revealing severe surface deterioration in PVA/MCC films, moderate degradation in PVA/SMCC, and minimal morphological changes in PVA/SMCC–ZnO films. Contact angle increased from 67.3° (PVA/MCC) to 86° (PVA/SMCC) and 92° (PVA/SMCC–ZnO), indicating enhanced hydrophobicity. Mechanical testing indicated that PVA/SMCC–ZnO possessed superior tensile strength with reduced elongation at break. Overall, the synergistic interaction of SMCC and ZnO significantly enhanced the barrier, antibacterial, and mechanical performance of PVA, underscoring their suitability for advanced packaging applications. title: Neuroprotective Efficacy of Chrysin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles Against Bisphenol-A-Induced Neurotoxicity
author: Soni, Hemant
abstract: CHR@C-NPs were successfully synthesised and comprehensively characterised. CHR@C-NPs significantly improved cognitive and neurobehavioral performance in BPA-induced rats compared to bulk chrysin. CHR@C-NPs attenuated oxidative stress by reducing MDA and Nitrate levels and restoring GSH levels and SOD activity. CHR@C-NPs ameliorated BPA-induced histopathological alterations in the hippocampus. Bisphenol-A (BPA), a widespread endocrine-disrupting contaminant, induces neurotoxicity through oxidative stress and neuronal apoptosis. This study developed chrysin-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (CHR@C-NPs) to facilitate delivery of chrysin to the brain, and evaluated their neuroprotective effects against BPA-induced neurotoxicity. CHR@C-NPs were synthesised by ionic gelation and characterised using UV–VIS, FTIR, SEM, TEM, and AFM. Male Wistar rats were randomly allocated into six experimental groups ( n  = 6): vehicle control, BPA-intoxicated, free chrysin, BPA + free chrysin, BPA + CHR@C-NPs, and blank chitosan nanoparticles. Cognitive function was assessed using the Morris water maze, Novel Object Recognition Test, and Open Field Test, alongside oxidative stress markers, antioxidant and hippocampal histology. CHR@C-NPs showed a mean particle size of ~ 199 nm, a zeta potential of + 22.9 mV, and > 55% encapsulation efficiency. SEM demonstrated spherical nanoparticles with aggregation upon drying, whereas TEM confirmed individual nanoparticles with an average diameter of 48 ± 11 nm. FTIR verified successful encapsulation of chrysin within the chitosan matrix, and AFM revealed a well-defined nanoscale surface topography. CHR@C-NPs significantly improved cognition, reduced oxidative stress, restored antioxidant defences, and preserved neuronal architecture, demonstrating neuroprotection against BPA-induced neurotoxicity compared with bulk chrysin. Graphical Abstract

title: Recent advances in microbial enzyme systems for paddy straw bioconversion and composting
author: Keerthana, R. S.
abstract: Paddy straw is one of the most abundant lignocellulosic agricultural residues generated worldwide, and its improper disposal through open-field burning contributes significantly to air pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, nutrient loss, and soil degradation. Sustainable management of paddy straw therefore requires efficient and eco-friendly biodegradation approaches. This review highlights the role of lignocellulolytic microorganisms and their enzyme systems in the biodegradation and valorization of paddy straw. The structural complexity of paddy straw, mainly due to cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin, limits natural degradation and necessitates the synergistic action of specialized microbial communities and extracellular enzymes. The review discusses the contributions of bacteria, fungi, and actinomycetes in producing cellulases, xylanases, pectinases, laccases, manganese peroxidase, and lignin peroxidase involved in lignocellulose breakdown. It also summarizes microbial mechanisms of degradation and the influence of substrate characteristics, environmental conditions, and microbial interactions on enzymatic efficiency. Special emphasis is placed on microbial consortia, pretreatment strategies, and recent advances in consortium engineering for accelerated decomposition and biomass valorization. Overall, the review provides a comprehensive understanding of sustainable paddy straw management through integrated microbial and enzymatic biotechnological approaches.

title: Controllable preparation and properties of carbon nanotube-based cattail-like high-efficient absorbing materials
author: Yang, Kequan
journal: Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics
abstract: The proliferation of radar systems and wireless communication has intensified electromagnetic pollution, endangering information security and public health, thereby precipitating an urgent need for advanced electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbers. Inspired by the natural “wave-trapping” structure of cattail seed heads, a novel cattail-like FeCo/N-doped carbon/CNT heterostructure was constructed in this study using carbon nanotubes as the matrix and dopamine as a binder to anchor magnetic particles, assisted by controllable dispersion and high-temperature calcination-induced in situ growth techniques. The results show that the composite achieves a minimum reflection loss of − 54.94 dB at 4.55 GHz. Moreover, at a matching thickness of only 2 mm, it exhibits an effective absorption bandwidth of 5.5 GHz with a reflection loss of − 46.21 dB. Radar cross-section (RCS) simulations further confirm its superior radar attenuation capability in practical applications, with the minimum radar scattering cross-section reaching − 41.01 dB·m^2. Radar cross-section simulations further confirm its robust attenuation capability for practical scenarios. The current research reports a simple bio-inspired strategy to overcome the impedance mismatch bottleneck of highly conductive carbon materials, facilitating the advancement of “thin, light, wide, and strong” microwave absorbers.

title: Numerical Investigations of Sisal Fiber Reinforced with PLA Composite Using Digimat Software
author: Yanda, Sagar
abstract: The automotive, construction, aerospace, marine, packaging, and electronics sectors all make extensive use of natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites due to its affordability, sustainability, and low weight. In order to assess mechanical and environmental performance, this study uses DIGIMAT software to model and simulate Sisal fiber composites. Because experimental testing is expensive, numerical analysis provides efficiency. Findings supported by the law of mixtures demonstrate that the mechanical characteristics of the composite are much improved by increasing the concentration of fiber weight, hence validating the efficacy of simulation-based material optimization. Graphical Abstract

title: MEYELens: An affordable, open-source, 3D-printable eyewear platform for pupillometry and gaze tracking
author: Vecchieschi, Giacomo
abstract: Pupillometry and gaze tracking provide sensitive, noninvasive indices of autonomic function and cognitive state and are increasingly employed in neuroscience and clinical research. However, commonly used systems remain costly and often constrain hardware customization and workflow transparency. MEYELens is presented as an open-source, fully 3D-printable wearable system for low-cost pupillometry and gaze tracking using readily available components. The design is modular and mechanically adjustable to accommodate different users and experimental requirements. An open pipeline is provided for data acquisition and for both offline and online analysis. Feasibility is demonstrated across frequency-based and task-evoked pupillary paradigms, and gaze mapping is shown to operate in both screen-based and naturalistic settings. By combining affordability, modular hardware, and open software, MEYELens reduces barriers to reliable eye-based measurement and supports methodological development in resource-constrained research contexts.

title: Raman reporters for SERS/SERRS biosensing and biomedicine: design, applications, and challenges
author: He, Hengzhou
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and surface-enhanced resonance Raman scattering (SERRS) offer molecular fingerprint specificity, high sensitivity, narrow spectral bandwidths, and multiplex readout capability for biosensing and biomedical analysis. In reporter-encoded SERS/SERRS nanotags, Raman reporters are key signal-generating molecules that define spectral identity, context-dependent brightness, stability, multiplexing capacity, and quantitative reliability. However, existing reviews have mainly focused on plasmonic substrates, nanotag architectures, assay formats, imaging applications, or spectral-analysis workflows, whereas reporter molecules themselves have been less systematically discussed as molecular and interfacial design variables. This review provides a focused, reporter-centered synthesis of conventional, aromatic thiol/disulfide, Raman-silent-region, near-infrared-resonant/SERRS, responsive, and library-based reporters. We discuss reporter selection principles, reporter–core interactions, immobilization chemistry, surface coverage and orientation, spectral orthogonality, responsive-reporter metrics, multiplex unmixing, machine-learning-assisted spectral decoding, biomolecular scaffolds, and whole-nanoprobe safety. By integrating molecular design, interfacial stability, quantitative performance evaluation, and translational constraints, this review aims to support rational Raman reporter selection, benchmarking, and application-specific deployment. Graphical Abstract

title: Synthesis of chitosan-encapsulated mono- and di-metallic (Zn/Ca) MOFs to modulate seed quality and antioxidant defense in Chenopodium quinoa under salinity stress
author: Mahmoud, Noura E.
abstract: Soil salinity is a major environmental constraint that severely limits the growth and nutritional yield of Chenopodium quinoa Willd. Although metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show strong potential in agricultural settings, hybridizing them with biopolymers facilitates application under environmental conditions. This study aimed to develop a novel biostimulant by synthesizing chitosan-encapsulated mono-metallic (Zn-MOF) and di-metallic (Zn/Ca-MOF) frameworks and evaluating their efficacy in quinoa under saline field conditions. The composites were synthesized and characterized for their structural and chemical properties. Quinoa plants were cultivated under saline field conditions and treated with chitosan-MOF composites to assess physiological and biochemical responses, with a focus on nutritional value and the antioxidant defense system. Our findings revealed that application of the chitosan–MOF composites—most notably the bimetallic Zn/Ca formulation—substantially enhanced plant growth, biomass accumulation, and physiological performance under saline field conditions. Treatment with the composite enhanced the accumulation of key nutritional constituents in the seeds, specifically increasing the relative proportions of phytosterols, unsaturated fatty acids, and essential amino acids. Furthermore, application of the composite enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities (including SOD and POD), which was accompanied by a marked reduction in lipid peroxidation (45%) and hydrogen peroxide levels (57%). These physiological improvements corresponded to significant gains in plant biomass and seed quality parameters under saline field conditions. Overall, this study demonstrates that chitosan-encapsulated di-metallic frameworks serve as an effective, multi-functional strategy for enhancing salt tolerance in quinoa, offering a sustainable approach to improving crop resilience and food security in saline environments.

title: Symptom prevalence and pharmacological management of late-stage Parkinson’s disease (LSPD): a cross-sectional, multinational survey
author: Pallauf, Christine
